title: In the city — asking the way and getting around
goal: Ask where something is, understand the answer, and take the metro, bus, or taxi without getting lost.
bekal: ask "where is…" and understand the directions you're given
take an Iranian taxi, which works differently from taxis back home

dialogs.title: گفتگو — راهِ موزه
dialogs.intro: Budi is lost in downtown Tehran and asks a man who is waiting for the bus.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: Excuse me, sir, where is the National Museum?

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: سلام. نزدیک است. پیاده ده دقیقه.
lines.baca: salâm. nazdik ast. piyâde dah daghighe.
lines.id: Hello. It's close. A ten-minute walk.
lines.literal: hello. near is. on-foot ten minute.

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: مستقیم بروید تا چهارراه، بعد دست چپ بپیچید.
lines.baca: mostaghim beravid tâ chahârrâh, ba'd dast-e chap bepichid.
lines.id: Go straight to the intersection, then turn left.
lines.literal: straight go-you up-to four-way, after hand-of left turn-you.

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: از خیابانِ سی تیر بالا بروید. موزه سمتِ راست است.
lines.baca: az khiyâbân-e Si Tir bâlâ beravid. muze samt-e râst ast.
lines.id: Go up Si Tir Street. The museum is on the right.
lines.literal: from street-of Si Tir up go-you. museum side-of right is.

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: دقیقاً! در تهران بالا یعنی شمال، طرفِ کوه.
lines.baca: daghighan! dar Tehrân bâlâ ya'ni shomâl, taraf-e kuh.
lines.id: Exactly! In Tehran "up" means north, toward the mountains.
lines.literal: exactly! in Tehran up means north, direction-of mountain.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: چه راحت! با مترو هم می‌شود رفت؟
lines.baca: che râhat! bâ metro ham mishavad raft?
lines.id: How handy! Can I take the metro too?
lines.literal: what easy! with metro also becomes go?

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: بله، ایستگاهِ امام خمینی. ولی پیاده نزدیک‌تر است.
lines.baca: bale, istgâh-e Emâm Khomeyni. vali piyâde nazdiktar ast.
lines.id: Yes, Imam Khomeini station. But walking is quicker.
lines.literal: yes, station-of Imam Khomeini. but on-foot nearer is.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: Thank you so much. That's very kind of you.

lines.speaker: رهگذر:
lines.text: خواهش می‌کنم. اگر گم شدید، دوباره بپرسید.
lines.baca: khâhesh mikonam. agar gom shodid, dobâre beporsid.
lines.id: You're welcome. If you get lost, just ask again.
lines.literal: request do-I. if lost become-you, again ask-you.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: I will. Have a nice day.

notes: **The word کجاست = کجا + است.** The same merger as چیست and کیست in unit 3. The spoken form is کجاست too — one of the few words that doesn't change.

⚠️ **In Tehran, "up" means north and "down" means south.** The city leans against the slopes of the Alborz mountains, so its northern part really is higher. Tehranis say بالا شهر ("uptown", the wealthier north) and پایین شهر ("downtown"), and everyday directions use بالا and پایین without naming compass points at all. Know this, and half of all directions in Tehran suddenly make sense.
**"Can one go?" = می‌شود رفت؟** A set pattern meaning "is it possible": می‌شود اینجا سیگار کشید؟ ("can I smoke here?"), می‌شود کمکم کنید؟ ("could you help me?"). Memorize it whole now.
**"That's very kind of you" = لطف کردید**, literally "you did a kindness". A warmer thank-you than plain ممنون, used when someone has really gone out of their way for you.
**"Have a nice day" = روزِ خوبی داشته باشید** and **"take care, safe travels" = به سلامت** (literally "with safety"). Two polite, warm goodbyes; both are worth memorizing whole.
**Spoken forms:** موزهٔ ملی کجاست؟ (unchanged), مستقیم برین (*mostaghim berin*), دست چپ بپیچین (*dast-e chap bepichin*), می‌شه رفت؟ (*mishe raft?*). Notice ـید → **ـین** and می‌شود → **می‌شه**.

grammars.title: Asking the way and understanding the answer
after: **If the directions come too fast, one sentence saves you:** می‌شود رویِ نقشه نشان بدهید؟ (*mishavad ru-ye naghshe neshân bedahid?*, "could you show me on the map?"). Almost any Iranian will pull out a phone and show you themselves.

grammars.title: Commands: بـ + present stem
after: **Always use the شما form (ـید) with people you don't know well.** The bare تو form sounds like an order to a small child.
**Don't:** replace بـ with نـ — نرو ("don't go"), نگویید ("don't say"), نگران نباشید ("don't worry").
To soften a command, add لطفاً at the start or end: لطفاً بنشینید، صبر کنید لطفاً. And the most polite of all is بفرمایید, which you've had since unit 5.

blocks.text: Notice the ending **ـگاه** ("place") that forms many place names: ایستگاه ("stopping place" = stop, station), فرودگاه ("landing place" = airport), دانشگاه ("knowledge place" = university), آرامگاه ("resting place" = tomb), خوابگاه ("sleeping place" = dormitory). Like ـخانه in unit 5, it makes long words guessable.
The four compass points — شمال، جنوب، شرق، غرب — are Arabic loanwords. If you've ever met "Maghreb" ("the west") or "Mashriq" ("the east"), you've already seen two of their relatives.

blocks.title: Three things about the Tehran metro
items: **Cheap, fast, and free of the traffic jams** that make car trips three times longer. For newcomers, it's the easiest way to get around — signs are in Persian and English.
**There are women-only cars** (واگنِ ویژهٔ بانوان) at the front and back of the train. Women may choose any car; men may not enter the women-only ones.

**The ride-hailing apps اسنپ (Snapp) and تپ‌سی (Tapsi)** work like the apps you know, but both need an Iranian phone number. That's one reason the SIM card from unit 6 is the first thing you should buy.
Excuse me, where is the museum?

exercises.prompt: Make the polite command form (the شما form).
Fill in the right direction or place word.
items: The place where you wait for the bus: ____
In Tehran, the everyday word for north: ____
A taxi you hire just for yourself: تاکسیِ ____

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: ببخشید، موزه کجاست؟ — مستقیم بروید تا چهارراه. — دستِ چپ بپیچید. — از اینجا دور است؟ — گم شده‌ام.
